characterList.description: The speaker, a young man with short dark hair, wearing glasses and a black button-down shirt. Sometimes seen wearing black pants and shoes, or standing behind a podium.
characterList.name: Vivek Sahaedevan Nair

content_metadata.description: Vivek Sahaedevan Nair discusses his journey of innovation, from facing academic and financial constraints to developing a technology that can potentially transform carbon emissions into valuable carbon nanotubes, offering both environmental and economic benefits.

qAndA.answer: They told him that he would have no job after four years in the Bioengineering field and that his only hope would be to get a job in some IT company.
qAndA.question: What did Vivek’s senior colleagues tell him about the job prospects in his field on his first day of college?

qAndA.answer: He wanted to make a biosensor out of them.
qAndA.question: Why did Vivek initially want to purchase a few hundred grams of carbon nanotubes?
What was the price of carbon nanotubes per gram?

qAndA.answer: His professor had allowed him to experiment with the chemical but had forbidden him from working after 5 PM. Therefore, he had to take the chemicals back to his hostel and work on the substrate in his room and later, the backyard of his hostel.
qAndA.question: Why did Vivek need to conduct his experiment with cement and sand in secret?

qAndA.answer: He believed that it would have a huge, global impact on reducing carbon emissions and transforming them into a valuable product with many applications.
qAndA.question: What kind of environmental impact did Vivek hope his technology would have if widely adopted?

youtube_description:
http://inktalks.com Vivek Nair presents a promising solution to check air pollution at its source, and at the same time produce a valuable resource. Nair has devised a process that converts harmful carbon emissions into carbon nanotubes, a material stronger than steel and more expensive than gold.

ABOUT INK: INKtalks are personal narratives that get straight to the heart of issues in 18 minutes or less. We are committed to capturing and sharing breakthrough ideas, inspiring stories and surprising perspectives--for free!

Watch an INKtalk and meet the people who are designing the future--now.
http://INKtalks.com

ABOUT VIVEK NAIR:
Vivek Nair had stumbled upon a process to convert carbon emissions into carbon nanotubes (a material stronger than steel). His discovery led him to start a company focused on automating this process and turning carbon emission into a useable resource for many applications. Vivek was named one of the today's disruptors and tomorrow's brightest stars by Forbes "30 under 30" list,for the year 2012 & MIT Technology Review outstanding innovators under 35, for the year 2012.He has also received the National award for meritorious invention from NRDC, Gov. of India. Vivek has also been named by Tehelka as "Tipping point - Architects of the Future", for the year 2012. He was also the winner of Ashoka/Staples Social Youth Entrepreneur award.  In addition, Vivek is doing his double doctorate in Materials Science and Mechanical Engineering at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore & Loughborough University, UK to further his effort in developing advanced materials of the future.
